name: Calexico
label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
lede: Giant Sand's rhythm section named their side project after a border town, filled it with mariachi horns, pedal steel and Tucson heat, and outgrew the band that made them.

hero.by: Photo: Moses Namkung, Outside Lands 2009. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Giant Sand's rhythm section
eras.text: Joey Burns was a music student at UC Irvine when he met John Convertino, the drummer in Howe Gelb's Giant Sand. The two became a rhythm section for hire, backing Victoria Williams, Richard Buckner, Barbara Manning and Bill Janovitz, until their own songs started piling up.

years.h: Joey Burns meets John Convertino and ends up in Giant Sand
years.p: Burns first plays upright bass with Gelb's band on a European tour, then joins. He and Convertino lock in as a pair.

years.src: Wikipedia: Friends of Dean Martinez · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: Friends of Dean Martinez put out an album on Sub Pop
years.p: Burns and Convertino play in the Tucson side project with steel guitarist Bill Elm. The Shadow of Your Smile comes out on Sub Pop in 1995.

years.h: The duo records Spoke over November and December
years.p: The record is self-titled in effect: at this point the band itself is called Spoke.

years.h: Spoke comes out in Germany, 2,000 copies on Hausmusik
years.p: A limited first edition on the German indie label. The same year Burns and Convertino split from Bill Elm and Friends of Dean Martinez.
years.xp: AllMusic later gave the album three stars and called it "a Santa Fe rummage sale of sounds."

eras.title: Named for a border town
eras.text: Touch and Go's Quarterstick imprint signed the duo, and the band took the name of Calexico, the California town on the Mexican line. Three albums in four years turned a side project into the main event, and Giant Sand paid for it.

years.h: Quarterstick signs Spoke, and Spoke becomes Calexico
years.p: The label reissues Spoke in the US under the new name. Burns and Convertino also make Slush as OP8 with Gelb and Lisa Germano.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Black Light · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: The Black Light maps the desert from Tucson to Mexico
years.p: A concept album about the desert of Arizona and northern Mexico, cut at Wavelab in Tucson and at Burns's and Convertino's homes. The Wall Street Journal's critic rated it one of the year's best.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Uncut 9 out of 10. AllMusic called it deeper and richer than the debut.

The band built its audience the slow way, opening for [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], [[Dirty Three|af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4]] and [[Lambchop|f75150f0-d80d-4c34-903b-6acfb47b63ee]]. In 1999 it sold The Road Map, a limited CD, only at its own shows.

years.h: Hot Rail brings in the trumpets
years.p: Horns and violin arrive, with [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]] on cornet among the guests. Entertainment Weekly gave it an A-minus and Pitchfork 7.9.

years.h: Burns and Convertino quit Giant Sand for Calexico
years.p: By 2000 the two bands wanted the same two people. Burns and Convertino played on Giant Sand's Chore of Enchantment, then left Gelb's band to do Calexico full time.
years.xp: Gelb told the Arizona Daily Star that Giant Sand "began losing a lot of momentum" after they left, and described a "sea of silence" between himself and Burns. The paper notes that Calexico and Giant Sand had never shared a bill.

eras.title: A touring band, then a masterpiece
eras.text: Calexico grew from a duo into a band of six on stage, with two trumpeters, a pedal steel player and a German bassist. Feast of Wire was the payoff, and the collaborations started to come.

years.cap: Calexico at the AStA Sommerfest, Frankfurt
years.src: Internet Archive: Calexico Live at Paradiso · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: Paul Niehaus's first full tour on pedal steel reaches Amsterdam
years.p: At the Paradiso, Burns and Convertino are joined by trumpeters [[Martin Wenk|2ca607a0-7bb3-4fd1-a2af-d342d99087b9]] and [[Jacob Valenzuela|79278a18-d848-4288-ba89-c2359b29da87]], bassist [[Volker Zander|2b904662-78eb-48b7-a9f2-3fa8829ced6e]] and [[Paul Niehaus|f84893b8-2c33-4218-adc4-4169954610d8]].
years.xp:
The taper's notes for the Paradiso show mark it as the first full tour with Niehaus on pedal steel. Shannon Wright sat in on vocals.

Mariachi Luz de Luna, who often played live with the band, appear on the 2001 rarities set Even My Sure Things Fall Through. Aerocalexico was sold only at gigs that year, and "Ballad of Cable Hogue" turned up in the German comedy Lammbock.

years.h: Two Frenchmen and two Tucsonans make Tête à Tête as ABBC
years.p: Burns and Convertino record with Naïm Amor and Thomas Belhôm at the end of 2000. The album comes out on Wabana in 2001.

years.cap: Calexico at the Capitol, Offenbach, Germany, April 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: Feast of Wire · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: Feast of Wire is the one Pitchfork had been waiting for
years.p: Sixteen tracks from Wavelab, co-produced with engineer Craig Schumacher. Metacritic's average lands at 86.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Joe Tangari gave it 8.9 and called it "the album we always knew they had in them but feared they would never make." Mojo praised the arrangements as the band's most ambitious.

The limited edition added covers of the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]'s "Corona", Françoiz Breut's "Si tu disais" and Link Wray's "Fallin' Rain".

years.cap: Calexico at a Lincoln Park festival, Chicago, June 2004
years.h: Love and the Minutemen get the mariachi treatment on Convict Pool
years.p: The EP covers [[Love|34ec9a8d-c65b-48fd-bcdd-aad2f72fdb47]]'s "Alone Again Or" with flamenco handclaps and Swedish singer Nicolai Dunger, and gives "Corona" horns that recall "Ring of Fire".

years.cap: Calexico and Iron & Wine at Manchester Academy
years.src: Wikipedia: In the Reins · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: Sam Beam writes, Calexico plays: In the Reins
years.p: [[Iron & Wine|c3f28da8-662d-4f09-bdc7-3084bf685930]]'s Beam wrote all seven songs and both bands recorded them at Wavelab. The EP reaches No. 135 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: Fewer horns, more Dylan, last records for Touch and Go
eras.text: Garden Ruin dropped the instrumentals and leaned on songs. Calexico became the go-to backing band for a Dylan film, and then Touch and Go, its home for a decade, shut down manufacturing and distribution.

years.h: Garden Ruin is Calexico's first album with no instrumentals
years.p: Produced with JD Foster, it trades the indie-mariachi tag for direct, guitar-and-vocal songs. By 2009 it had sold 46,000 copies in the US.

years.h: Paul Niehaus gets a co-write on "Nom de Plume"
years.p: The pedal steel player shares the credit with Burns on the Garden Ruin track.

years.src: Wikipedia: I'm Not There · Wikipedia: In the Reins · Arizona Daily Star
years.h: Willie Nelson, Roger McGuinn and Charlotte Gainsbourg sing Dylan with Calexico
years.p: The I'm Not There soundtrack uses Calexico behind five singers, plus two of its own instrumental themes for the film.
years.xp:
The pairings: Jim James on "Goin' to Acapulco", Iron & Wine on "Dark Eyes", Roger McGuinn on "One More Cup of Coffee", Willie Nelson on "Señor (Tales of Yankee Power)" and Charlotte Gainsbourg on "Just Like a Woman". Calexico also recorded "Main Title Theme (Billy)" and "Bunkhouse Theme".

Burns also appears on Iron & Wine's The Shepherd's Dog, released the same year.

years.h: Sergio Mendoza joins on keys, accordion and percussion
years.p: The Tucson musician becomes a core member and, eight years later, a co-producer.

years.h: Carried to Dust goes gold in Europe
years.p: Guests include Iron & Wine, [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]]'s [[Douglas McCombs|2bf77a32-29bb-432f-afe1-bde92b431c23]], Pieta Brown and Amparo Sanchez. The independent labels' association certified it gold in 2012 for 75,000 European sales.
years.xp: AllMusic gave it 4.5 stars, calling it the band's most balanced record. The tour that followed covered the US, the British Isles and Western Europe.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · Wikipedia: Calexico
years.h: Touch and Go shuts its distribution arm
years.p: Corey Rusk announces the label will downsize and stop manufacturing and distribution, citing the economy. Carried to Dust is Calexico's last new album through it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Calexico · Internet Archive: Calexico Live at Serenadenhof
years.h: The six-piece takes Carried to Dust to Golden Gate Park
years.p: In August the 2001 lineup, with Jairo Zavala added on guitar, plays Nuremberg's Serenadenhof and San Francisco's Outside Lands. The same year, "Banderilla" turns up in an episode of Breaking Bad.

eras.title: Anti-, New Orleans, and a house on the coast
eras.text: Calexico moved to Anti- in the US and kept City Slang in Europe. The records got more open to guests and places, from a New Orleans neighborhood to a rented house on the Northern California coast.

years.cap: Calexico at the Vancouver Folk Music Festival, July 2010
years.h: A documentary score, and the West Coast with Arcade Fire
years.p: Calexico releases the soundtrack to the documentary Circo and spends part of the year touring the US west coast with [[Arcade Fire|52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68]].

years.h: "Slowness" wakes the crew of Space Shuttle Endeavour
years.p: Tucson congresswoman Gabby Giffords dedicates the Carried to Dust song to her husband, astronaut Mark Kelly, as the wake-up song on Endeavour's final flight.

years.h: Algiers is named for the New Orleans neighborhood where it was made
years.p: Calexico's seventh studio album and its first on Anti- in the US, with City Slang in Europe.

years.h: Edge of the Sun fills the room with guests
years.p: [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]], Sam Beam, Ben Bridwell, Gaby Moreno, Carla Morrison and members of Greek group Takim all appear. Mendoza co-produces with Burns and Convertino.

years.h: Calexico records in a coastal house it calls the Phantom Ship
years.p: The Thread That Keeps Us is made at Panoramic House in Northern California with longtime engineer Craig Schumacher co-producing.
years.xp: "There's a little more chaos and noise in the mix than what we've done in the past," Burns said. The album debuted at No. 2 on Billboard's Alternative Albums retail chart and No. 7 in Germany.

eras.title: Iron & Wine again, and Feast of Wire at twenty
eras.text: Two decades on, Calexico made a full album with Sam Beam, a holiday record and a Latin-leaning set from Mendoza's studio, then took its best-known record back on the road.

years.cap: Calexico and Iron & Wine at Festival du Bout du Monde, France, 2019
years.h: Fourteen years after In the Reins, a full album with Iron & Wine
years.p: Years to Burn, announced in March, comes out on Sub Pop, the label where Burns and Convertino started out with Friends of Dean Martinez.

years.h: Seasonal Shift, a Calexico holiday album
years.p: Anti- and City Slang put it out ahead of the holidays.

years.h: El Mirador arrives in April
years.p: Calexico announced the album in February and released it on April 8.

years.cap: Calexico at the San Javier Jazz Festival, Spain
years.h: Feast of Wire comes back for its twentieth birthday
years.p: The band reissues the 2003 album and tours it, taking the anniversary shows into 2024.

yt: Joey Burns on Feast of Wire, 13th Floor, 2023
years.h: Three nights in New Zealand for the anniversary tour
years.p: Wellington on February 9, Christchurch on the 10th, Auckland on the 11th. Burns previewed the shows talking Feast of Wire, Shane MacGowan and Barbara Manning with 13th Floor.
